# 12-Week Muscle Gain Programme

**Client profile:** 26 years old, strict vegan, recreational lifter, full gym access
**Goal:** Hypertrophy (muscle gain)
**Nutrition target:** 150 g protein/day from plant sources only
**Structure:** Four training days per week, split into an upper/lower pattern, progressing through three four-week phases

---

## Overview of Phases

| Phase | Weeks | Focus | Rep Range | Intensity (RIR*) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Foundation | 1–4 | Movement quality, work capacity, base volume | 10–15 | 3–4 RIR |
| 2. Hypertrophy | 5–8 | Volume accumulation, progressive overload | 8–12 | 2–3 RIR |
| 3. Intensification | 9–12 | Heavier loads, peak volume, consolidation | 6–10 | 1–2 RIR |

*RIR = reps in reserve. Stop each set with that many reps left in the tank.

**Weekly template (all phases):**
- Day 1: Upper A
- Day 2: Lower A
- Day 3: Rest or active recovery (walking, mobility)
- Day 4: Upper B
- Day 5: Lower B
- Days 6–7: Rest

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Learn patterns, establish baseline loads, build tissue tolerance. Keep technique crisp and leave a reserve on every set.

### Upper A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Dumbbell bench press | 3 × 10–12 | Controlled eccentric, 2 s lowering |
| Seated cable row | 3 × 10–12 | Full stretch at the start, squeeze at the end |
| Dumbbell shoulder press | 3 × 10–12 | Neutral grip if shoulder is sensitive |
| Lat pulldown | 3 × 10–12 | Lead with elbows |
| Cable lateral raise | 2 × 12–15 | Light, strict |
| Incline dumbbell curl | 2 × 10–12 | Full stretch |
| Overhead cable triceps extension | 2 × 10–12 | Keep elbows tight |

### Lower A
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 3 × 10–12 | Depth to comfortable range, tempo 3-1-1 |
| Romanian deadlift (dumbbell or barbell) | 3 × 10–12 | Hinge at hips, soft knees |
| Leg press | 3 × 12–15 | Feet mid-platform |
| Seated leg curl | 3 × 12–15 | Slow eccentric |
| Standing calf raise | 3 × 12–15 | Full range, pause at the top |
| Plank | 3 × 30–45 s | Neutral spine |

### Upper B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Incline dumbbell press | 3 × 10–12 | 30° incline |
| Chest-supported row | 3 × 10–12 | Squeeze shoulder blades |
| Cable chest fly | 3 × 12–15 | Constant tension |
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 3 × 10–12 each | Brace on bench |
| Face pull | 3 × 12–15 | External rotation at the end |
| Hammer curl | 2 × 10–12 | Neutral grip |
| Rope pushdown | 2 × 12–15 | Full lockout |

### Lower B
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Hip thrust (barbell or machine) | 3 × 10–12 | Full hip extension, pause at top |
| Bulgarian split squat | 3 × 8–10 each | Front shin vertical-ish |
| Leg extension | 3 × 12–15 | Pause at lockout |
| Lying leg curl | 3 × 12–15 | Hips flat |
| Seated calf raise | 3 × 12–15 | Full stretch |
| Dead bug | 3 × 8 each side | Slow, controlled |

**Progression rule:** When you hit the top of the rep range on all sets with good form, increase load by the smallest available increment (usually 2–2.5 kg for upper body, 5 kg for lower body).

---

## Phase 2: Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Increase weekly volume and load. Add one set to the main compound lifts and keep accessories the same.

### Changes from Phase 1
- Main compounds (bench/incline press, row, squat/leg press, RDL, hip thrust): **4 sets** instead of 3
- Rep ranges shift to **8–12**
- Effort increases to **2–3 RIR**
- Add a **drop set** on the final set of one isolation exercise per session (e.g., cable lateral raise, leg extension, cable fly). Drop weight 20–25% and perform to failure.

### Upper A and B, Lower A and B
Use the same exercise selections as Phase 1, with the adjustments above.

### Weekly Load Guidance
Aim to add weight or reps across each main lift roughly every 1–2 weeks. If a lift stalls for two consecutive sessions, reduce load by 5–10% and rebuild.

**Deload check (end of Week 8):** If she reports persistent fatigue, poor sleep, joint discomfort, or stalled performance across multiple lifts, take Week 8 at roughly 60% of normal volume (drop to 2 sets per exercise) before Phase 3.

---

## Phase 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–12)

**Goal:** Push heavier loads and peak volume. Consolidate gains.

### Changes from Phase 2
- Main compounds: **4 sets × 6–8 reps** on the primary lift each session, with secondary compounds at 3 × 8–10
- Effort increases to **1–2 RIR**
- Rest periods extend to **2–3 minutes** on compounds
- Isolation work stays at 10–15 reps
- Replace Phase 2 drop sets with **rest-pause** on one isolation exercise per session (perform to near failure, rest 15 s, continue for 2–3 mini-sets)

### Primary Lifts by Session
| Session | Primary Lift | Secondary Lift |
|---|---|---|
| Upper A | Barbell or dumbbell bench press | Lat pulldown or pull-up |
| Upper B | Incline dumbbell press | Chest-supported or single-arm row |
| Lower A | Back squat or leg press | Romanian deadlift |
| Lower B | Hip thrust (barbell) | Bulgarian split squat |

**Week 12:** Test performance on the primary lifts (a top set at target RIR) to measure progress. Retake body weight and, if available, circumference measurements.

---

## Nutrition Guidance (Plant-Based, 150 g Protein/Day)

Hitting 150 g of protein from plants requires deliberate planning. Plant proteins are generally less leucine-dense and somewhat less digestible than animal proteins, so aim for the upper end of the range and use a variety of sources.

**Protein distribution:** Four meals of roughly 35–40 g, spaced 3–5 hours apart, with the largest meal post-training.

**Key protein sources (approximate protein per serving):**
- Seitan (100 g): ~25 g
- Tofu, firm (150 g): ~20 g
- Tempeh (100 g): ~19 g
- Soy milk (250 ml): ~7 g
- Pea protein powder (30 g scoop): ~20–24 g
- Lentils, cooked (100 g): ~9 g
- Chickpeas, cooked (100 g): ~7 g
- Edamame (100 g): ~11 g
- Hemp seeds (30 g): ~10 g
- Quinoa, cooked (185 g): ~8 g
- Oats (80 g dry): ~10 g
- Nutritional yeast (15 g): ~8 g

**Sample day (~150 g):**
- **Breakfast:** Overnight oats with soy milk, 40 g pea protein, hemp seeds, berries (~45 g)
- **Lunch:** Tempeh grain bowl with quinoa, edamame, chickpeas, greens (~40 g)
- **Pre/post-workout snack:** Smoothie with soy milk, pea protein, banana (~30 g)
- **Dinner:** Seitan stir-fry with lentil noodles or rice, tofu, vegetables (~45 g)

Total: roughly 160 g. Adjust portions to the client's calorie needs.

**Calories:** A surplus of roughly 250–400 kcal/day above maintenance supports lean gain. Estimate maintenance first, then track weekly body weight. Aim for a gain of about 0.25–0.5 kg/week; adjust if it falls outside that range.

**Other considerations:**
- Check **B12** status (supplement 25–100 µg daily or as advised) and consider a vitamin D, iron, zinc, iodine, and omega-3 (algae-based DHA/EPA) review with her GP or a dietitian.
- Creatine monohydrate (3–5 g/day) is well supported for lifters and is vegan-friendly.
- Fortified plant milks and cereals help meet calcium needs.

---

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. Prioritise this above all else.
- **Hydration:** Roughly 35 ml/kg body weight daily, more on training days.
- **Active recovery (Day 3):** 20–40 minutes of brisk walking, light cycling, or mobility work.
- **Deload:** As described in Phase 2.
- **Warm-up:** 5 minutes of light cardio plus 2 ramp-up sets before each main lift.

---

## Tracking

- Log every session: loads, reps, RIR.
- Weigh her 3–4 times weekly under the same conditions and use the weekly average.
- Take photos and measurements every four weeks.
- Reassess at Week 12 and plan the next block.

---

**Note for you as the trainer:** Before starting, screen for injuries, medical conditions, and medications, and consider a referral to a registered dietitian for the B12 and micronutrient review, particularly since the protein and calorie targets are demanding on a plant-only diet.

# Cardio Add-On for the 12-Week Muscle Gain Programme

Cardio supports heart health, work capacity, and recovery between sessions. The aim here is to add it without compromising muscle gain, so the plan keeps cardio low-to-moderate in intensity and keeps the total volume modest. Her calorie surplus should cover the extra energy cost.

---

## Principles

- **Keep most cardio low-intensity (Zone 2)**, which is conversational pace and interferes least with strength and hypertrophy.
- **Limit high-intensity intervals to one session per week**, placed away from heavy lower-body days.
- **Total weekly cardio: about 90–150 minutes**, scaled up gradually across phases.
- **Separate cardio from lifting where possible.** If done on the same day, lift first.

---

## Weekly Structure (Updated)

| Day | Session | Cardio |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Upper A | 10 min easy bike or treadmill warm-up only |
| Day 2 | Lower A | 10 min easy bike warm-up only |
| Day 3 | Active recovery | 30–40 min Zone 2 walk, cycle, or row |
| Day 4 | Upper B | 15–20 min Zone 2 post-lift (optional) |
| Day 5 | Lower B | Rest from cardio |
| Day 6 | Cardio session | 20–30 min Zone 2 or 1 HIIT session (see below) |
| Day 7 | Rest or easy walk | 20–30 min easy walk |

---

## Phase Progression

### Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
- **Zone 2 sessions:** 2 × 25–30 min (Day 3 and Day 6)
- **Post-lift cardio:** Optional 10–15 min on Day 4
- **HIIT:** None; focus on building aerobic base
- **Weekly total:** ~60–75 min
- **Modality:** Incline walking, stationary bike, rowing machine at easy pace

### Phase 2: Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)
- **Zone 2 sessions:** 2 × 30–40 min (Day 3 and Day 6)
- **Post-lift cardio:** 15 min on Day 4
- **HIIT:** Introduce 1 session per week on Day 6 from Week 6 onward (see protocol below)
- **Weekly total:** ~90–110 min
- **Week 8 deload:** Reduce cardio duration by about 40%, drop HIIT.

### Phase 3: Intensification (Weeks 9–12)
- **Zone 2 sessions:** 2 × 30–40 min (Day 3 and Day 7)
- **Post-lift cardio:** 10–15 min on Day 4, or drop if recovery is poor
- **HIIT:** 1 session per week on Day 6
- **Weekly total:** ~100–130 min
- **Priority:** Protect recovery for heavy top sets. If primary lift performance drops for two consecutive sessions, cut HIIT first.

---

## Session Protocols

**Zone 2 (steady-state):**
- Intensity: conversational pace, around 60–70% of max heart rate (roughly RPE 3–4 out of 10)
- Modality options: incline treadmill walk, stationary bike, elliptical, rowing machine
- Check: she should be able to speak in full sentences

**HIIT (Phase 2 onward, one session per week):**
- Warm-up: 5 min easy
- Work: 30 s hard (RPE 8/10) / 90 s easy, repeated 8 times (about 12 min of work period)
- Cool-down: 5 min easy
- Modality: bike or rower (low impact, easy to control intensity)
- Progress to 10 rounds in Phase 3 if recovery allows

**Post-lift cardio (Day 4):**
- Keep it short and easy, 10–15 min on bike or treadmill
- Purpose is to aid recovery, not to add fatigue

---

## Nutrition Adjustment

Cardio adds energy expenditure, so recheck her calorie target:
- If she is doing 90–130 minutes per week of cardio, add roughly 100–150 kcal/day to her maintenance estimate, or hold the surplus at 250–400 kcal above her adjusted maintenance.
- Protein stays at 150 g/day. Cardio does not change protein needs, but extra carbohydrate around sessions helps fuel HIIT and Zone 2 work. Oats, rice, quinoa, and fruit work well.
- Keep fluid intake higher on cardio days, roughly an extra 500 ml.

---

## Monitoring

- **Weekly body weight trend:** Confirm she's still gaining about 0.25–0.5 kg/week. If gain stalls, reduce cardio before increasing food.
- **Recovery markers:** Track resting heart rate and sleep. A consistent rise in resting heart rate or drop in sleep quality signals too much cardio.
- **Performance:** If primary lift numbers drop for two consecutive weeks, reduce HIIT first, then Zone 2 duration.

---

**Note for you as the trainer:** If she has no cardiovascular history, consider a brief health screen (such as PAR-Q+) before starting HIIT, and adjust intensity to her heart rate response and perceived effort.

## What to look for

- **Vegan certification** (e.g. Vegan Society trademark or equivalent), since some products use whey or are made on shared equipment with dairy.
- **Protein content of at least 20 g per 30 g serving** (roughly 65–80% protein by weight). Avoid products heavy in carbs, fillers, or sugar if your goal is protein density.
- **Leucine content of about 2–2.5 g per serving.** Plant powders are often lower in leucine than whey, so a soy-pea blend or one with added leucine helps close that gap. Check the label, since many brands list amino acids.
- **Complete amino acid profile.** Soy is complete on its own. Pea is low in methionine, so blending pea with rice or soy gives a fuller profile.
- **Third-party testing** (e.g. Informed Sport, NSF Certified for Sport, or Labdoor ratings) to reduce the risk of contamination or undeclared ingredients, which matters for anyone training competitively or regularly.
- **Simple ingredient list** with minimal artificial sweeteners and no proprietary blends that hide dosages.

## Good options to consider (check current formulations)

- **Soy protein isolate:** Complete, cost-effective, high leucine. Good default for most clients.
- **Pea-rice or pea-soy blends:** Better amino acid balance and often well tolerated. Good if she dislikes soy.
- **Pea protein isolate with added leucine:** Useful if she prefers pea and wants to boost leucine per scoop.

Avoid recommending a specific brand as a blanket endorsement without checking the current label, since formulations change.

## Practical notes

- **Start with one or two scoops per day** and fit them around meals so total protein reaches 150 g. Using a scoop in the breakfast smoothie and post-workout is a simple pattern.
- **Check for digestive tolerance.** Pea and soy can cause bloating for some people, so a trial of one product for 1–2 weeks before committing is sensible.
- **Watch for added creatine or pre-workout blends** if she is already taking creatine separately; doubling up is unnecessary and can be costly.
- **Ask her about soy allergy or sensitivity** before choosing soy, and about any thyroid conditions, since large amounts of soy are sometimes discussed in that context. Moderate intake from whole and isolated soy is generally considered safe, but it's worth confirming with her doctor if relevant.

# Cheat Meal Day Add-On

A planned cheat meal can help a client stick to a demanding plan, especially on a plant-based diet that can feel restrictive around social eating. For her, the goal is to make it a structured, controlled part of the programme rather than an open-ended break from it.

---

## Principles

- **One planned meal or one flexible meal per week, not a full day of unrestricted eating.** This keeps the calorie surplus intact and prevents a week of gains being undone.
- **Keep protein on track.** Anchor the meal with a protein source so it still contributes toward the 150 g target.
- **Stay fully vegan.** Vegan junk food, takeaway, and desserts are widely available, so the cheat meal doesn't need to break her dietary rules.
- **Schedule it strategically.** Place it on a day after heavy training (such as after Lower B or a primary-lift session) when glycogen replenishment is most useful.
- **Plan it, don't reward or punish with it.** Framing it as a planned flexible meal reduces guilt and binge risk.

---

## Structure

| Week | Cheat meal | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| 1–4 | Optional, one flexible meal on Day 5 or Day 7 | After Lower B or on rest day |
| 5–8 | One flexible meal on Day 5 | After Lower B (heavy lower session) |
| 9–12 | One flexible meal on Day 5, with an optional second on Day 7 if recovery and body weight trend are on track | After Lower B |

Skip the cheat meal in Week 8 if the deload is in effect, and in Week 12 if she is doing testing.

---

## Vegan Cheat Meal Ideas

Each is roughly 800–1,100 kcal and still includes a protein anchor of 30–40 g.

1. **Vegan burger and loaded fries:** Plant-based patty (pea or soy, ~20 g protein), wholemeal bun, vegan cheese, and a side of baked sweet potato fries.
2. **Pizza night:** Two slices of thin-crust vegan pizza with soy or seitan toppings and a side salad.
3. **Takeaway curry with rice and naan:** Chickpea or tofu curry (check it's vegan-made), basmati rice, and a shared vegan dessert.
4. **Vegan dessert pairing:** A soy-based dessert or a dark chocolate and soy-yogurt bowl with fruit, alongside a regular meal.
5. **Ramen or pho:** Tofu or seitan broth bowl with noodles and edamame.

---

## Keeping It on Track

- **Calorie accounting:** Log the meal roughly. Do not try to hit precise targets on this day. Maintain the weekly average surplus instead.
- **Hydration:** Drink water with the meal, especially with high-sodium takeaway.
- **Next-day plan:** Return to normal eating the following day without compensating by skipping meals or adding extra cardio.
- **Watch for patterns:** If she tends to overeat once the meal starts, or it triggers guilt or restriction afterwards, drop it and use a flexible-eating approach instead. Consider referral to a registered dietitian if disordered eating is a concern.

---

**Note for you as the trainer:** Cheat meals work best when the rest of the week is consistent. If her body weight is gaining faster than 0.5 kg/week, reduce the frequency before cutting protein or training volume.

3. **Seitan and rice stir-fry** (~45 g, ~75 g carbs): seitan, jasmine rice, vegetables, low-sodium soy sauce, ginger, garlic, sesame oil.
4. **Lentil and chickpea curry** (~45 g, ~90 g carbs): red lentils, chickpeas, seared tofu, brown rice, spinach, chapati or vegan-checked naan.
5. **Black bean and quinoa burrito bowl** (~42 g, ~80 g carbs): quinoa, black beans, sweetcorn, crumbled tempeh, salsa, avocado.
6. **Lentil bolognese with pasta** (~40 g, ~85 g carbs): wholewheat or chickpea pasta, brown lentil sauce, nutritional yeast, side salad.
7. **Soba noodle bowl** (~40 g, ~85 g carbs): soba, edamame, baked tofu, vegetables, tamari-sesame dressing. Good after HIIT or heavy leg days.

### Supplements and micronutrients
- **Vitamin B12:** Daily supplement (25–100 µg) or as advised by her GP or dietitian. Essential.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5 g/day, vegan-friendly and well supported for lifters.
- **Review with GP or dietitian:** Vitamin D, iron, zinc, iodine, and algae-based omega-3 (DHA/EPA).
- **Calcium:** Use calcium- and B12-fortified soy milk.

---

## 8. Cheat Meal Schedule

**Format:** One planned flexible meal per week on Day 5, after Lower B. It should be vegan, anchored with a protein source (30–40 g), and roughly 800–1,100 kcal. Do not turn it into a full unrestricted day.

**Examples:** Vegan burger with sweet potato fries; thin-crust vegan pizza with soy or seitan toppings; takeaway chickpea or tofu curry with basmati and naan; ramen or pho with tofu and edamame; a vegan dessert alongside a regular meal.

**Schedule:**
- Weeks 1–4: Optional
- Weeks 5–7: Yes
- Week 8 (deload): No
- Weeks 9–11: Yes, with an optional second meal on Day 7 if recovery and weight trend are on track
- Week 12 (testing): No

**Rules:**
- Log it roughly. Do not chase precise targets.
- Return to normal eating the next day. Do not skip meals or add cardio to compensate.
- If it triggers overeating, guilt, or restriction, drop it. Consider a dietitian referral if disordered eating is a concern.

---

## 9. Recovery and Tracking

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. Below 7 hours on several nights is a signal to cut the final primary set before cutting cardio.
- **Hydration:** About 35 ml/kg/day, plus roughly 500 ml extra on cardio days.
- **Active recovery (Day 3):** Zone 2 cardio, mobility, or easy walking.
- **Resting heart rate:** A sustained rise signals too much training stress.
- **Logging:** Record loads, reps, and RIR for every session.
- **Body weight:** Weigh 3–4 times per week under the same conditions and use the weekly average.
- **Photos and measurements:** Every four weeks and at Week 12.
- **Performance:** Track the primary lifts weekly. Use Week 4 and Week 12 as benchmarks.

---

## 10. Trainer Notes

- **Before starting:** Complete a health screen (PAR-Q+ or equivalent), check injury history and medications, and confirm she has no cardiovascular or thyroid issues before HIIT and high soy intake.
- **Referral:** A registered dietitian should review her B12 and micronutrient status and check that the plan meets her needs on a plant-only diet.
- **Calorie estimates** are starting points. Adjust them from her actual weight trend, not from the formulas.
- **Phase 3 intensity** assumes solid barbell technique. Scale back the final-set effort if she is newer to heavy lifting.
- **Plan review at Week 12:** Compare testing against Week 4 and Week 8 benchmarks, then design the next block.

# 12-Week Muscle Gain Programme (Consolidated)

**Client:** 26 years old, strict vegan, recreational lifter, full gym access
**Goal:** Muscle gain (hypertrophy) with a lean surplus
**Training:** 4 sessions per week (Upper/Lower split), plus cardio
**Nutrition:** 150 g protein/day from plant sources only

---

## 1. Week-by-Week at a Glance

| Week | Phase | Lifting | Cardio | Cheat meal | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Foundation | 3 sets, 10–15 reps, 3–4 RIR | Zone 2 ×2 | Optional (Day 5) | Establish baseline loads |
| 2 | Foundation | As Week 1 | Zone 2 ×2 | Optional (Day 5) | Add load when top of range is hit |
| 3 | Foundation | As Week 1 | Zone 2 ×2 | Optional (Day 5) | Same |
| 4 | Foundation | As Week 1 | Zone 2 ×2 | Optional (Day 5) | Re-test baseline reps |
| 5 | Hypertrophy | 4 sets compounds, 8–12 reps, 2–3 RIR, drop set | Zone 2 ×2 | Yes (Day 5) | Volume increases |
| 6 | Hypertrophy | As Week 5 | Zone 2 + HIIT starts | Yes (Day 5) | First HIIT session |
| 7 | Hypertrophy | As Week 5 | Zone 2 + HIIT | Yes (Day 5) | Watch recovery |
| 8 | Hypertrophy (deload) | 2 sets per exercise, ~60% volume | Zone 2 −40%, no HIIT | No | Deload |
| 9 | Intensification | Push version: 5×5–6 primary, 0–1 RIR final set | Zone 2 + HIIT (10–12 rounds) | Yes (Day 5) | Heavier loads begin |
| 10 | Intensification | As Week 9, final set pushed | Zone 2 + HIIT | Yes (Day 5) | Peak volume |
| 11 | Intensification | As Week 9 | Zone 2 + HIIT | Yes (Day 5) | Peak load |
| 12 | Intensification (test) | Reduced volume, top set 3–5 at 1 RIR | Zone 2 only, reduced | No | Testing week |

---

## 2. Weekly Template

| Day | Session | Cardio |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Upper A | 10 min easy bike warm-up |
| Day 2 | Lower A | 10 min easy bike warm-up |
| Day 3 | Active recovery | Zone 2, 25–30 min (Wks 1–4), 30–40 min (Wks 5–8), 35–40 min (Wks 9–12) |
| Day 4 | Upper B | Optional post-lift Zone 2, 10–15 min |
| Day 5 | Lower B | No cardio. Cheat meal after training (where scheduled) |
| Day 6 | Cardio | Zone 2, 25–30 min (Wks 1–5); HIIT from Week 6 onward |

Warm-up before every lift: 5 minutes light cardio, then 2 ramp-up sets on the first main lift (3 ramp-up sets in Phase 3).

---

## 3. Phase 1: Foundation (Weeks 1–4)

**Goal:** Learn movement patterns, set baseline loads, build tissue tolerance. Leave 3–4 reps in reserve on every set.

## 4. Phase 2: Hypertrophy (Weeks 5–8)

**Goal:** Increase weekly volume and load.

### Changes from Phase 1
- Main compounds (bench/incline press, row, squat/leg press, RDL, hip thrust): **4 sets**
- Rep range: **8–12**
- Effort: **2–3 RIR**
- **Drop set** on the final set of one isolation exercise per session (drop load 20–25%, take to failure)
- Accessories stay at Phase 1 selections

### Sessions
Use the Phase 1 exercise selections with the changes above. Primary compound sets go from 3 to 4.

### Load guidance
Add weight or reps on main lifts every 1–2 weeks. If a lift stalls for two consecutive sessions, drop load 5–10% and rebuild.

### Week 8: Deload
- Two sets per exercise (about 60% of normal volume)
- Zone 2 duration reduced by about 40%
- No HIIT, no cheat meal
- Keep protein at 150 g

Trigger an earlier deload if she reports persistent fatigue, poor sleep, joint discomfort, or stalled performance across multiple lifts.

- **Week 12 (testing):** Warm up, then work to a top set of 3–5 reps at 1 RIR on the primary lifts. Reduce accessory volume to about 2 sets each. Retest body weight and measurements.
- **Guardrail:** If form breaks down or she misses reps on two consecutive sessions, drop the final set of the primary lift and keep the rest of the session.
- **Beginner caveat:** If she is newer to heavy barbell work, keep the final set at 1–2 RIR instead of 0–1.

## 6. Cardio Protocols

**Zone 2 (steady state):**
- Conversational pace (about RPE 3–4/10, roughly 60–70% max HR)
- Modalities: incline walk, stationary bike, elliptical, rower
- Duration: 25–30 min (Wks 1–5), 30–40 min (Wks 6–8), 35–40 min (Wks 9–12)

**HIIT (Weeks 6–12, Day 6 only, one session per week):**
- 5 min easy warm-up
- Work: 30 s hard (RPE 8/10) / 90 s easy
- Rounds: 8 (Weeks 6–8), 10–12 (Weeks 9–12)
- 5 min easy cool-down
- Modality: bike or rower
- Cut to 6–8 rounds if recovery drops

**Post-lift cardio (Day 4, optional):** 10–15 min easy bike or treadmill. Keep it short. Drop it if recovery is poor.

**Cardio priority:** If performance drops for two consecutive sessions, reduce HIIT first, then Zone 2 duration. Protect strength volume.

## 7. Nutrition

### Calories
1. Estimate maintenance (for example, using bodyweight × 30–33 kcal, then adjust to her activity level).
2. Add 100–150 kcal/day to account for cardio.
3. Add a surplus of 250–400 kcal/day on top of that.
4. Track weekly average body weight (3–4 weigh-ins per week). Target gain: **0.25–0.5 kg/week**. Adjust the surplus if the trend falls outside that range.
5. If gain stalls in Phase 3, add 100–150 kcal/day from carbohydrate around training. Do not cut protein.

### Protein: 150 g/day
- **Distribution:** Four feeds of 35–40 g, spaced 3–5 hours apart, with the largest feed after training.
- Use a soy or pea-based powder to cover 30–40 g of protein per day.

### Protein powder
- **Type:** Soy protein isolate (good default), pea-rice or pea-soy blend (better amino acid balance, good if she dislikes soy), or pea isolate with added leucine.
- **Look for:** Vegan certification, at least 20 g protein per 30 g serving, about 2–2.5 g leucine per serving, third-party testing (Informed Sport, NSF Certified for Sport), simple ingredient list.
- **Trial:** Test one product for 1–2 weeks to check for bloating before committing.
- **Use:** One or two scoops per day, in breakfast and post-workout.
- **Check:** She should not be doubling up with creatine or pre-workout blends.

### Breakfast options (35–45 g protein)
1. **Tofu scramble on wholegrain toast** (~42 g): 200 g firm tofu with turmeric, nutritional yeast, black salt; 2 slices wholegrain toast; spinach, peppers, tomatoes; fortified soy milk latte.
2. **Protein overnight oats** (~45 g): 80 g oats, 250 ml soy milk, 30 g protein powder, 30 g hemp seeds, berries, nut butter. Prepare the night before.
3. **Tempeh breakfast hash** (~40 g): 120 g tempeh, 150 g roasted potato or sweet potato, peppers, onion, kale, smoked paprika, 150 g black beans.
4. **Chickpea flour pancakes** (~38 g): 80 g chickpea flour, 200 ml soy milk, mushrooms and spinach, avocado, 100 g edamame.
5. **Smoothie bowl** (~40 g): 300 ml soy milk, 30 g protein powder, banana, berries, 30 g hemp seeds, granola.

### Post-workout meals (35–45 g protein, higher carbohydrate after HIIT or heavy lower-body days)
1. **Protein smoothie bowl** (~45 g protein, ~70 g carbs): soy milk, protein powder, banana, berries, hemp seeds, peanut butter, granola, kiwi.
2. **Hummus and edamame wrap** (~40 g, ~60 g carbs): wholemeal tortilla, hummus, edamame, pan-fried tempeh, slaw, fruit.
3. **Seitan and rice stir-fry** (~45 g, ~75 g carbs): seitan, jasmine rice, vegetables, low-sodium soy sauce, ginger, garlic, sesame oil.
4. **Lentil and chickpea curry** (~45 g, ~90 g carbs): red lentils, chickpeas, seared tofu, brown rice, spinach, chapati or vegan-checked naan.
5. **Black bean and quinoa burrito bowl** (~42 g, ~80 g carbs): quinoa, black beans, sweetcorn, crumbled tempeh, salsa, avocado.
6. **Lentil bolognese with pasta** (~40 g, ~85 g carbs): wholewheat or chickpea pasta, brown lentil sauce, nutritional yeast, side salad.
7. **Soba noodle bowl** (~40 g, ~85 g carbs): soba, edamame, baked tofu, vegetables, tamari-sesame dressing. Good after HIIT or heavy leg days.

### Supplements and micronutrients
- **Vitamin B12:** Daily supplement (25–100 µg) or as advised by her GP or dietitian. Essential.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5 g/day, vegan-friendly and well supported for lifters.
- **Review with GP or dietitian:** Vitamin D, iron, zinc, iodine, and algae-based omega-3 (DHA/EPA).
- **Calcium:** Use calcium- and B12-fortified soy milk.

## 8. Cheat Meal Schedule

**Format:** One planned flexible meal per week on Day 5, after Lower B. It should be vegan, anchored with a protein source (30–40 g), and roughly 800–1,100 kcal. Do not turn it into a full unrestricted day.

**Examples:** Vegan burger with sweet potato fries; thin-crust vegan pizza with soy or seitan toppings; takeaway chickpea or tofu curry with basmati and naan; ramen or pho with tofu and edamame; a vegan dessert alongside a regular meal.

**Schedule:**
- Weeks 1–4: Optional
- Weeks 5–7: Yes
- Week 8 (deload): No
- Weeks 9–11: Yes, with an optional second meal on Day 7 if recovery and weight trend are on track
- Week 12 (testing): No

**Rules:**
- Log it roughly. Do not chase precise targets.
- Return to normal eating the next day. Do not skip meals or add cardio to compensate.
- If it triggers overeating, guilt, or restriction, drop it. Consider a dietitian referral if disordered eating is a concern.

## 9. Recovery and Tracking

- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours. Below 7 hours on several nights is a signal to cut the final primary set before cutting cardio.
- **Hydration:** About 35 ml/kg/day, plus roughly 500 ml extra on cardio days.
- **Active recovery (Day 3):** Zone 2 cardio, mobility, or easy walking.
- **Resting heart rate:** A sustained rise signals too much training stress.
- **Logging:** Record loads, reps, and RIR for every session.
- **Body weight:** Weigh 3–4 times per week under the same conditions and use the weekly average.
- **Photos and measurements:** Every four weeks and at Week 12.
- **Performance:** Track the primary lifts weekly. Use Week 4 and Week 12 as benchmarks.

## 10. Trainer Notes

- **Before starting:** Complete a health screen (PAR-Q+ or equivalent), check injury history and medications, and confirm she has no cardiovascular or thyroid issues before HIIT and high soy intake.
- **Referral:** A registered dietitian should review her B12 and micronutrient status and check that the plan meets her needs on a plant-only diet.
- **Calorie estimates** are starting points. Adjust them from her actual weight trend, not from the formulas.
- **Phase 3 intensity** assumes solid barbell technique. Scale back the final-set effort if she is newer to heavy lifting.
- **Plan review at Week 12:** Compare testing against Week 4 and Week 8 benchmarks, then design the next block.
